characterList.description: A male with a brown skin tone wearing a white lab coat.
characterList.name: Scientist

content_metadata.description: This video demonstrates the preparation and inoculation of an API strip for bacterial identification, including preparing a purity plate.

qAndA.answer: The water creates a humidified chamber to prevent the API strip from drying out during incubation.
qAndA.question: Why does the scientist fill the base of the API strip with water?

qAndA.answer: Nine cupules are topped up with liquid paraffin.
qAndA.question: How many cupules are topped up with liquid paraffin?

qAndA.answer: Sterilizing the wire ensures that no contaminating bacteria are introduced into the distilled water or the API strip.
qAndA.question: Why does the scientist sterilize the straight wire before inoculating the sterile distilled water?

qAndA.answer: A blood agar plate is used, indicated by its red color.
qAndA.question: What type of agar plate is used for the purity plate?

qAndA.answer: The streaking pattern progressively dilutes the bacterial sample, allowing for the isolation of individual bacterial colonies for further analysis.
qAndA.question: Why does the scientist streak the purity plate in a specific pattern?

scenes.contextualRelevance: The video starts with clear learning objectives, setting the stage for a practical demonstration of using API strips in microbiology.
scenes.title: Introduction and Learning Objectives

videoEditingDetails.description: Title slide: 'Introduction to using API strips (Analytical Profile Index) in microbiology.' and 'Teaching resources from the Microbiology Laboratory' by Marilena Ioannou.
Slide with learning objectives: 'Learning objectives and what you will see:' followed by six bullet points outlining the steps involved in using API strips.

Inoculating a bacterial colony into sterile distilled water

characterInteraction.description: The scientist interacts with the viewers by explaining the steps involved in preparing the API strip and bacterial suspension.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Emphasis on sterilization and even bacterial suspension for test results.

narrativeProgression.description: The scientist starts by labeling the API strip.
He fills the base of the strip with water to create a humidified chamber.
The scientist selects a single bacterial colony from a Petri dish.
He mixes the bacterial suspension thoroughly.

He checks for any air bubbles in the filled microtubes.

Preparing a purity plate by streaking a bacterial suspension sample

He tops up the designated cupules with paraffin oil.
Explanation and demonstration of the streaking technique.

climax.description: The climax is reached when the scientist completes streaking the purity plate, marking the completion of the preparation process.

http://www.biologycourses.co.uk

API strips 1 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=umD3QFwNAkU
API strips 2 http://youtu.be/qfs2bByiYXU
API strips 3 http://youtu.be/1wuGuOlFZlo

This video introduces you to API strips which are used for the identification of microorganisms including bacteria and yeast. The strips provide a quick and reliable means of testing and the "strip" is a series of wells consisting of different biochemical tests. The video shows how to use a bacterial inoculum to seed the wells and prepare the strip for incubation.
